segments.t: The Discounters is a German comedy set in a supermarket in Hamburg. On his first day at work, Titus tells the camera why he has come. This short taster simplifies his introduction for beginners. Listen to the German first; you do not need to catch every word.
Ja, ich bin Titus.
Heute ist mein erster Tag hier.
Die anderen kenne ich noch nicht so gut.
Aber ich bin nicht hier, um Freunde zu finden.
Ich bin hier, um Geld zu verdienen.
Let's unpack his introduction, his first day, and his reason for taking the job.
Ja, ich bin Titus.

'Yes, I'm Titus.' This is a direct self-introduction. The two words before his name identify who he is. Keep that opening and replace the name with your own when introducing yourself. The first little word simply adds an affirmative yes; it is not part of his name.
Heute ist mein erster Tag hier.

'Today is my first day here.' German can put the time expression first. The verb still takes the second position, before the subject phrase. Notice the ending on the word for first: it belongs with the masculine noun for day. The possessive tells us whose first day this is.
Die anderen kenne ich noch nicht so gut.

'I don't know the others very well yet.' The opening points to the other employees. Knowing people means being familiar with them; knowing a fact would call for a different German word. The two words expressing not yet leave room for that familiarity to grow. His final two words soften the description: he does not know them all that well.
Aber ich bin nicht hier, um Freunde zu finden.

'But I'm not here to make friends.' The opening marks a contrast with what we might expect from someone starting a new job. After the comma, he names the purpose he is rejecting; the earlier negative tells us it is not his aim. Literally he says finding friends; natural English usually says making friends. The plural refers to friends in general, rather than one particular friend.
Ich bin hier, um Geld zu verdienen.

'I'm here to earn money.' Listen for the purpose construction again. Its opening word introduces his goal; the little marker just before the final action word completes it. The money comes between those two markers. Both parts concern the same person: Titus is here, and Titus intends to earn the money. This sentence gives the practical reason for his new job. Now listen to the entire short introduction once more.
Ja, ich bin Titus.
Heute ist mein erster Tag hier.
Die anderen kenne ich noch nicht so gut.
Aber ich bin nicht hier, um Freunde zu finden.
Ich bin hier, um Geld zu verdienen.

Titus is starting a job, with earning money firmly in mind. You have practised introducing yourself, describing a first day, saying that you do not know people yet, and explaining a purpose. See you next time!
Tschüss!
